mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar non-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when both proxies move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer spending (HOUST) above 1% of previous month's level coincides with a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%), signaling a shift toward demand-driven growth that supports S&P 500 gains in the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1% above prior month and CPIAUCSL < 2% from prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from a neutral baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months below 100 suggests supply-side constraints, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar contraction regimes (walk-forward simulation).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.5% while the 1-month change in the S&P 500 5-day return is negative, it indicates a mispricing of inflation risk that precedes a short-term S&P 500 decline over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month > 0.5% and S&P 500 5-day return month-over-month < 0
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months is associated with stronger labor market conditions that predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than during comparable periods of stable unemployment (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (HOUST) and personal income (PAYEMS) above trend suggest robust consumer demand, which typically precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > trend and PAYEMS > trend in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite proxies moving in predicted direction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of S&P 500 5-day returns exceeds +2%, it indicates over-optimism in the market that tends to reverse in the next 20 days, producing negative returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) when 3-month MA > +2%.
